thinking: The detection bias toward the right side is likely caused by stricter thresholds that only well-defined, dense features (common on the right) can satisfy. The 'sparser' left side likely contains fragmented or shorter segments that fail the original 100-pixel minLineLength_oblique and the 50-vote hough_threshold_oblique. By lowering these to 70 and 35 respectively, and increasing maxLineGap_oblique to 60, we allow the detector to capture and bridge weaker features. Increasing dilation_iterations to 2 further supports this by thickening sparse points to improve connectivity before the Hough transform. Finally, widening the angle ranges to [5, 11] and [-11, -5] accounts for potential geometric perspective shifts on the tunnel periphery that might push the left-side segments slightly out of the original narrow 3-degree windows.
